title: What publishEvent actually does
summary: Four steps: wrap the payload, maybe buffer it, loop over matching listeners on the current thread, then hand the event to the parent context.
entry: Put a breakpoint in SimpleApplicationEventMulticaster.multicastEvent and publish anything. Look at the call stack: your business method is still on it, which is the entire point.

steps.notice: Read all four branches. A non-ApplicationEvent payload gets wrapped, early events get buffered, then the multicaster runs, and finally the event is republished to the parent context. Events travel up, never down.
A for loop with a null check. taskExecutor is null unless you set it, so listeners run inline; errorHandler is null too, so a listener exception comes straight back out of publishEvent.
Type matching plus a cache keyed by event type and source type. This is where a generic event silently fails to match a listener, because erasure removed the type argument.

Not on the publish path, but the reason your listener exists at all. It runs once after every singleton is created and walks bean definitions, which is why a @Lazy bean still gets its listeners registered.
Condition evaluation, argument resolution, reflective call, and the return-value handling that republishes whatever your listener returned as a brand new event.
Three branches and one of them is the bug you will hit: no active transaction, not a fallback listener, so it logs at DEBUG and returns without doing anything.
